sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The visa lets the de facto partner or spouse of an Australian citizen, Australian permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen, live in Australia permanently. It is usually granted to people who hold a temporary Partner visa (subclass 309).

sections.heading: Overview > You must
sections.text:
- hold a temporary Partner (Provisional) visa (subclass 309) or Dependent Child visa (subclass 445)
- in most cases, continue to be in a genuine and ongoing relationship with your sponsor.

Help with your visa

If you are getting help with your visa, make sure you read information on Who can help with your visa application.

sections.heading: Overview > With this visa you can
sections.text:
In addition to what you can do on your subclass 309 visa, you can:

- live, work and study in Australia indefinitely
- sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia
- apply for Australian citizenship if eligible.

sections.heading: Overview > Cost
sections.text: You paid for this visa when you made your applications for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.

sections.heading: Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
Processing times for Partner visa applications vary. Partner visa applicants may experience longer processing times than expected. For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

The processing time for a permanent Partner visa starts from the date of eligibility. This is two years after you applied for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.

Applications are processed according to Ministerial Direction 117. For more information, see Family visa processing priorities.

You can find the answers to common questions about Partner visa processing times at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

sections.heading: About this visa > With this visa you can
sections.text:
- live, work and study in Australia indefinitely
- access Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare
- sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia
- travel to and from Australia for 5 years
- if eligible, attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program
- if eligible, apply for Australian citizenship.

sections.heading: About this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a permanent visa.

You become a permanent resident on the day we grant the visa.

sections.heading: About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You and your family members must meet all visa conditions and obey Australian laws.

For more information see Check visa details and conditions.

sections.heading: About this visa > Travel on this visa
sections.text:
You can travel to and from Australia as many times as you want for 5 years from the date we grant this visa. This is as long as the travel facility on this visa is valid.

If you want to travel after the initial 5-year travel facility you must apply for and be granted a Resident Return (RRV). This will allow you to travel to Australia as a permanent resident.

To see when your travel facility ends, use VEVO.

First entry arrival date

If you are outside Australia at the time of visa grant, you must enter Australia before the first entry arrival date (first entry, arrive by) specified in your grant letter.

sections.heading: About this visa > Include family members
sections.text:
You can include members of the family unit in your application when you apply for the temporary Partner visa (subclass 309). Members of the family unit who apply with you must also be outside Australia

To include a dependent child in your permanent Partner visa (subclass 100) application after we have granted you a subclass 309 visa, your child must first apply for a Dependent child visa (subclass 445). We can grant your child the subclass 100 visa if they are members of the family unit and meet all other criteria.

You cannot add any family members after we grant the permanent Partner visa (subclass 100).

Dependent Child visa (subclass 445) holders

If you have a dependent child who does not hold a subclass 309 visa, you can add them to your permanent Partner visa (subclass 100) application before we make a decision on your permanent visa application.

Your child must hold a Dependent Child visa (subclass 445) and can be in or outside Australia.

Once your child holds a subclass 445 visa, complete and attach to your ImmiAccount, Form 1002 - Application by a subclass 445 dependent child for a permanent partner visa.

After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

Newborn children

If you have a baby after you have applied for this visa, you will need to let us know. For more information, see You had a baby.

sections.heading: About this visa > Cost
sections.text:
You paid for this visa when you applied for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.

You might have to pay other costs for health or police checks.

sections.heading: About this visa > Processing times
sections.text:
The processing time for a permanent Partner visa starts from the date of eligibility. This is 2 years after you applied for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.

We update processing times regularly. We assess all applications on a case by case basis. Complex cases may take longer to process. You should use published processing times as a guideline only.

Your application can take longer to process if:

- you do not fill it in correctly
- you don't include all required documents
- we need more information from you
- it takes time to verify your information.

sections.heading: About this visa > Visa label
sections.text: You will not get a label in your passport. We will digitally link your visa to your passport and create a digital visa record for you.

sections.heading: About this visa > Frequently asked questions
sections.text: You can find the answers to common questions about this visa at Partner Program Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of these criteria to be eligible for this visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Visa requirements
sections.text:
You must hold either a Partner (Provisional) (subclass 309) or a Dependent Child (subclass 445) visa.

2 years must have passed since you applied for the subclass 309 and 100 visas for you to be eligible to be assessed for the permanent subclass 100 visa. You can check the date you submitted your application in ImmiAccount.

We might grant you the permanent subclass 100 visa in less than 2 years if either:

- you were in a long-term partner relationship with your sponsor when you applied for the subclass 309 and 100 visas
- your sponsor is, or was, the holder of a permanent humanitarian visa and before that permanent visa was granted, was in a married relationship or de facto relationship with you. You must have informed us about your relationship before that permanent visa was granted.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Continue to meet relationship requirements
sections.text:
You must continue to be the spouse or de facto partner of the same person who sponsored you for the temporary Partner visa.

You might still be eligible for the permanent visa if your relationship ends or your partner dies before we grant the permanent visa. For more information, see Your relationship has changed.

If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you. You may still be eligible for the grant of your permanent visa. For more information, see Domestic and family violence and your visa.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Meet our health requirement
sections.text:
You and any members of the family unit, including dependent children who apply for the visa with you, must continue to meet our health requirement. Family members who do not come with you to Australia might also need to meet our health requirement.

If you had health examinations for your subclass 309 visa, we will let you know if you need to undertake them again or if more health checks are needed.

For more information on health related risks to the Australian community including Polio see risks to public health.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Have no debts to the Australian Government
sections.text:
If you or any family members owe the Australian Government money, you or they must pay it back or arrange to pay it back.

This may include family members who do not come with you to Australia.

sections.heading: Eligibility > Best interests of the child
sections.text: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply
sections.text:
If we granted you a permanent Partner visa (subclass 100) immediately after we granted your temporary Partner visa (subclass 309), you do not have to provide these documents or do anything else. If we did not, you need to provide further documents.

To check which visa you currently hold, use VEVO.

sections.heading: Step by step > Before you apply > Get help with your application
sections.text:
You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf, relating to your visa application.

To appoint someone to receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient.

If you need help with your application, you can appoint someone to give you immigration assistance. A person who gives you immigration assistance can:

- discuss your application with us
- give us information
- send and receive correspondence about your application.

We treat any correspondence they send as if it came from you.

It is important to provide your own contact details in case we need to contact you directly about your application. The partner visa application form will ask you for your own phone number and email address.

If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be one of the following:

- a registered migration agent
- a legal practitioner
- an exempt person.

To appoint someone to provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

For more information, see who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents
sections.text:
You are eligible for consideration of the permanent Partner visa two years after you apply for the temporary and permanent Partner visas. You can check the date you submitted your application in ImmiAccount.

Once two years have passed since you first applied, you can submit your documents for the permanent stage of your Partner visa. Do not send them before this time.

Make sure you provide all required information with your application. Applications with all required information can be processed faster.

Ensure that all information you provide is accurate. As a visa applicant, you must prove your identity and provide true information with your application.

For more information, see Providing accurate information.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Identity documents
sections.text: Provide a copy of the pages of your most recent passport. It must show your photo, personal details, signature, passport issue and expiry dates.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Character documents
sections.text:
To show that you meet our character requirements you may need to provide a current Australian police certificate. You usually need to provide this police certificate for the permanent stage of your Partner visa if you did not attach one with your subclass 309 application.

We may ask you to provide a new Australian police certificate, if your previous certificate has expired. For immigration purposes, police certificates are valid for 12 months from the issue date.

We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police.

To get an Australian police certificate see National Police Checks.

You also need to provide an overseas police certificate from any country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more since the grant of your 309 visa.

To get an overseas police certificate, see Offices outside Australia.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Evidence of your relationship
sections.text:
You must provide evidence that you continue to be the spouse or de facto partner of the same person who sponsored you for the temporary Partner visa.

In support of your visa application, you can provide:

- relationship documents
- supporting evidence of your relationship.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Evidence of your relationship > Relationship documents
sections.text:
Attach to your ImmiAccount a Commonwealth statutory declaration form. This form must be completed by your sponsor with information about any of the following:

- Whether you and your spouse or de facto partner have a mutual commitment, to the exclusion of all others.
- Whether your relationship is genuine and continuing.
- Whether you live together, or don't live permanently apart.
- When your relationship began and how long you have lived together.
- The financial commitments you and your partner share.
- The nature of your household (including any joint responsibility for the care and support of children).
- The social aspects of your relationship.
- The nature of your commitment to each other.
- Your plans for the future.

If you are married, provide your marriage certificate or other evidence that your marriage is valid in Australia.

If you are a de facto partner, provide proof of your de facto relationship.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Evidence of your relationship > Supporting evidence of your relationship
sections.text:
To show you are still in a relationship with your partner, you can provide the below supporting evidence of your relationship.

Finances

Evidence you and your partner share financial matters. This evidence can include:

- joint mortgage or lease documents
- joint loan documents for major assets like homes, cars or major appliances
- joint bank account statements
- household bills in both names.

Your household

Evidence you and your partner share domestic matters. This evidence can include:

- a statement about how you share housework
- household bills in both names
- mail or emails addressed to you both
- documents that show joint responsibility for children
- documents that prove your living arrangements.

Social matters

Evidence that others know about your relationship.

You must provide statements from 2 witnesses who:

- are 18 years old or older
- know you and your spouse or de facto partner
- know about your relationship.

Statements from witnesses can be done by completing Form 888 – Supporting statement in relation to a Partner or Prospective Marriage visa application.

If the witness is an Australian citizen or permanent resident, provide evidence of this such as a passport or birth certificate.

Evidence can also include:

- joint invitations or evidence you go out together
- proof you have friends in common
- proof you have told government, public or commercial bodies about your relationship
- proof you do joint sporting, cultural or social activities together
- proof you travel together.

Commitment

Evidence you are committed to a long-term relationship with each other. This evidence must show that you:

- have knowledge of each other’s background, family situation or other personal details.
- have combined your personal matters
- stay in touch when apart
- are not related by family.

You can also provide the terms of your wills as evidence.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Family members
sections.text:
For every family member who currently holds a subclass 309 or 445 visa, provide copies of:

- their passport
- documents that show changes to their situation
- police certificates, if applicable, for dependents 16 years old or older.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Tell us if your details have changed
sections.text: See here for changes to your contact details, address or passport

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Changes to your situation
sections.text:
Tell us if things change after you apply but before we've made a decision.

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your marital or de facto status
- the birth of a child
- any other changes relevant to your application
- a request to withdraw your application.

For more information, see Change in your situation.

If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

sections.heading: Step by step > Gather and prepare your documents > Prepare your documents
sections.text:
Translate

Have all documents translated into English.

Provide original and translated documents in your application.

Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their:

- full name
- address and telephone number
- qualifications and experience in the language they are translating.

These details must be in English.

Scan or photograph

Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

The scans and photos must be clear enough to read.

If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file.

You do not need to have any documents certified.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa
sections.text:
You are eligible for consideration of the permanent Partner visa two years after you apply for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.

Submit your documents for the permanent stage of your Partner visa once two years have passed since you first applied. Do not attach them before this time.

Using our website and protections to your privacy

We take our obligation to protect your privacy seriously. We provide a secure online environment, but you can do more to ensure your personal safety online:

- Make sure you give us your contact details when you apply for your visa and tell us if they have changed. We may need to contact you directly even if you have:

- nominated your sponsor’s email address for all electronic correspondence
- appointed your sponsor or someone else to receive your correspondence as your authorised recipient
- appointed someone to give you immigration assistance.

- Protect your ImmiAccount, email account and passwords. Don’t share them with anyone.

For more information see Using our website.

sections.heading: Step by step > Apply for the visa > How to apply
sections.text:
- Login to ImmiAccount.
- Select ‘New application’.
- Select ‘Family’.
- Select ‘Stage 2 – Permanent Pattner Visa Assessment’.
- Attach documents.

Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing.

Clearly label your documents.

You can attach up to 100 documents for each person on your application.

The attachment limit cannot be increased.

If you reach the attachment limit for an applicant, you can attach more documents to other clients on the application.

For more information see Applying online in ImmiAccount.

Frequently asked questions

A list of common questions and answers is available at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply
sections.text:
You can track and manage your application using ImmiAccount.

For help managing your application in ImmiAccount, see Applying online in ImmiAccount.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Status updates
sections.text:
Do not contact us if your application is within the current standard processing time. We cannot provide any further updates on your application's progress. You can check the status of your visa application and if you have provided all supporting documents through ImmiAccount.

To see current standard processing times for this visa, see Global processing times. This estimated timeframe is based on how long it has taken to process recently decided applications. It does not guarantee that your application will be decided within the current standard processing timeframe.

As Partner applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount.

You can find the answers to common questions about this visa at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Attach more information
sections.text:
If you did not attach all required documents when you applied, attach them as soon as you can in ImmiAccount.

We might ask you to provide more information.

As Partner visa applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount.

For more information on attaching documents in ImmiAccount, see Applying online in ImmiAccount.

If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Add family members
sections.text:
You can add a dependent child to your application before we make a decision on your permanent visa application. Your child can be in or outside Australia and must:

- hold a Dependent Child visa (subclass 445)
- be members of the family unit
- meet our health requirement
- meet our character requirement if they are 16 years old or older.

Once your child holds a subclass 445 visa, complete and attach to your ImmiAccount, Form 1002 - Application by a subclass 445 dependent child for a permanent partner visa.

After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

Newborn children

If you have a baby after you have applied for this visa, you will need to let us know. For more information, see You had a baby.

After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Tell us if things change after you lodge your documents but before we have made a decision.

Things you need to let us know about include:

- changes to your marital or de facto status
- the birth of a child
- any other changes relevant to your application.

For more information, see Change in your situation.

If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > If your relationship ends
sections.text:
You may need to complete the Notification of Relationship Cessation form in ImmiAccount.

To confirm, check Your relationship has changed.

Your online safety

To ensure your personal safety online we recommend that you:

- change your ImmiAccount password as soon as possible
- do not use saved passwords to access your ImmiAccount
- change your email password or consider setting up a new email account.

To see how you can increase your personal safety you can use the eSafety Commissioner’s online safety checklist

If you do not have access to ImmiAccount, you can notify us directly using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

You might still be eligible for the permanent visa if your relationship ends or your partner dies. All information you provide is confidential.

If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you.

You may still be eligible for the grant of your permanent visa. For more information, see Domestic and family violence and your visa.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > No longer need help with your application
sections.text:
Let us know if you no longer want someone to:

- receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient
- provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person.

After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount , let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

For more information see Who can help you with your application.

sections.heading: Step by step > After you apply > Mistakes on your application
sections.text:
Let us know as soon as you can if you have made a mistake on your application.

For more information see After you apply.

If you are unable to update your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

sections.heading: Step by step > Visa outcome
sections.text:
You can be in or outside Australia when we decide on your permanent Partner visa.

We will let you know our decision in writing.

If we grant your visa, we will tell you:

- your visa grant number
- the date your visa starts
- your visa conditions

Keep a copy of this decision.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you why we refused the visa and whether you have a right to a review of the decision.

We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.

New step description

sections.heading: When you have this visa > What you can do on this visa
sections.text:
- live, work and study in Australia
- access Australia's public healthcare scheme, Medicare
- sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia
- travel to and from Australia for 5 years
- if eligible, attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program
- if eligible, apply for Australian citizenship.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > How long you can stay
sections.text:
This is a permanent visa.

You become a permanent resident on the day we grant the visa.

For more information, see Permanent resident.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Travel on this visa
sections.text:
You can travel to and from Australia as many times as you want for 5 years from the date we grant this visa. This is as long as the travel facility on this visa is valid.

If you want to travel after the initial 5-year travel facility you must apply for and be granted a Resident Return (RRV). This will allow you to travel to Australia as a permanent resident.

To see when your travel facility ends, use VEVO.

First entry arrival date

If you are outside Australia at the time of visa grant, you must enter Australia before the first entry arrival date (first entry, arrive by) specified in your grant letter.

You can travel to Australia with an expired first entry arrival date if your visa is still valid. Your visa may still be subject to cancellation before arrival or at the border.

To see if your visa is still valid, use VEVO.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > New Zealand passport holders
sections.text:
If an immigration officer processes your clearance at our border, tell them:

- you have a permanent Australian visa
- you do not want a Special Category visa (subclass 444)

If you do not tell them, you might be granted a 444 visa. Grant of a subclass 444 visa will override your permanent visa and might affect your eligibility for Australian citizenship.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Sponsor your family members to come to Australia
sections.text:
You cannot add family members to your visa application after we grant the permanent Partner visa (subclass 100).

As an Australian permanent resident, you might be able to sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia.

To find a visa for your family members, explore visa options.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Prove you have a visa
sections.text:
To prove you have a visa and show your conditions to someone, use VEVO.

Australian visas are digital. We do not put a visa label in your passport. Instead, we link your digital visa record to your passport.

Your visa number is contained in your visa grant letter. Use this number to access your digital visa record in VEVO.

Your digital visa record is also used by:

- airlines, to check your visa before you board your flight
- Australian government agencies, to check your identity and visa conditions
- employers, banks or other registered organisations, to check your visa conditions.

To get proof of your travel in and out of Australia, request your international movement records.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Working
sections.text: With this visa you will have full work rights and be protected by Australian workplace law. See your workplace rights and entitlements.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Studying
sections.text: With this visa you will be able to study in Australia. To find out what study you may be eligible for see StudyAssist.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Access Australian Government benefits
sections.text: You might have to wait to access certain Australian Government payments and benefits. Learn more about newly arrived residents' waiting periods from Services Australia.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Tell us if things change
sections.text:
Let us know if you get a new passport.

See what to do if you have a new passport.

sections.heading: When you have this visa > Become an Australian citizen
sections.text:
After a certain time, you may be eligible for Australian citizenship. Find out more about becoming a citizen.

For citizenship purposes, your permanent residency starts on either the day your visa was granted if you were in Australia or the day you first entered Australia on this visa after it was granted.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > You must
sections.text:
- be the same person who sponsored the applicant for their temporary partner visa
- continue to be married or in a de facto relationship with them

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > With this sponsorship you can
sections.text: - have your spouse or de facto partner live, work and study in Australia indefinitely

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > How long you can stay
sections.text: The visa applicant can stay permanently in Australia.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Overview > Processing time
sections.text:
Processing times for Partner visa applications vary. Partner visa applicants may experience longer processing times than expected. For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application.

The processing time for a permanent Partner visa starts from the date of eligibility. This is two years after the applicant applied for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.

Applications are processed according to Ministerial Direction 117. For more information, see Family visa processing priorities.

You can find the answers to common questions about Partner visa processing times at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Your obligations
sections.text:
You must sponsor your partner and their family members included in their application.

As a sponsor, you must assist your partner and their family members included in their application, financially and with their accommodation.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > How long sponsorship lasts
sections.text:
When your sponsorship ends will depend on where the visa applicants are when we grant their temporary partner visa.

Your sponsorship will end 2 years after:

- the visa is granted, if the applicants are in Australia at the time of grant, or
- their next arrival in Australia, if they are outside Australia at the time of grant.

This is the case even if we grant their permanent partner visa straight after their temporary partner visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > About this visa > Apply to sponsor
sections.text: You can be inside or outside Australia when you apply to sponsor.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility
sections.text: You must meet all of these criteria to be eligible to sponsor your spouse or partner.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Eligibility > Continue to be the applicant's spouse or de facto partner
sections.text:
You must continue to be the spouse or de facto partner who sponsored the applicant and any family members included in their application for the temporary partner visa.

Your sponsorship must be approved. This approval will be given during the processing of the applicant’s temporary visa.

sections.heading: Sponsor > Step by step > Provide your documents
sections.text:
You do not need to submit another application for sponsorship. However, you will need to provide additional documents.

Attach to your ImmiAccount, the personal details page of your most recent passport (showing your signature), or your Australian driver's licence.

Also attach a completed Commonwealth statutory declaration form with information about any of the following:

- Whether you and your partner have a mutual commitment with your spouse of de facto partner to the exclusion of all others.
- Whether your relationship is genuine and continuing.
- Whether you live together or don't live permanently apart.
- When your relationship began and how long you have lived together for.
- The financial commitments you and your partner share.
- The nature of your household (including any joint responsibility for the care and support of children).
- The social aspects of your relationship.
- The nature of your commitment to each other.
- Your plans for the future.

New step description

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Tell us if things change
sections.text: If your situation has changed, you need to tell us. For more information see Changes in your situation.

sections.heading: Sponsor > When you have this visa > Withdraw your sponsorship
sections.text:
You cannot withdraw as a sponsor after we grant the visa. For more information, see Your relationship has ended.

If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, there is support available. For more information, see Family Violence Provisions.
